caseno: Appeal From Appellate Decree No. 252 of 1965.
lawyer:
Md. Ismailuddin Sarkar-For the Appellants. 
M. A. Mannan-For the Respondents.
parties:
Madan Chand Gouthy and ors ------ Appellants.
Vs.
Mohammad Nurul Huda and ors ------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
2 The plaintiff-respondent Nos. 1 and 2 filed the mortgage suit for recovery of mortgage money. Their case inter alia was that the plaintiff No. 3 Nawab Ali Ahmed was the owner in possession with other co-sharers of the suit land and he borrowed Rs. 1599/-from one Tarani Mohan Gope, predecessor of pro-defendant Nos. 5 and 6 and executed a deed of mortgage to Tarani on 8.8.192 1 corresponding to 23rd Sraban 1328 B.S. in respect of his share in the suit land, vide Ext. 2. The money was to be repaid by Kartik 1329 B S Tarani sold the mortgage to Nazitunnessa, wife of the mortgagor Nawab Ali Ahmed by a registered kabala, dated 2-6-1938, vide Ext. 1 and handed over the mortgage document to Islazituanessa Mortgagr Nawab Ali Ahmed has paid money on account of interest to Tarani and Nazitunnessa on various dates and he wrote the endorsement vide Ext. 3 series on the back of the mortgage deed Ext, 2 Nazitunessa died leaving her husband Nawab All Ahmed, plaintiff No. 2, and her son plaintiff No 1 as her only heir who became owners of the mortgage of the suit holding. The superior landlord Bridhi Chand Gouthi, auction purchased the suit holding in a rent sale, but no notice under section 167 of the Bengal Tenancy Act was served upon the plaintiffs of Tarani or anybody else to annul the encumbrance. So the mortgage still subsists. Al-though the plaintiff No. 2 mortgaged the suit land possession remained with him all throughout. After rent purchase Bridhi Chand Gouthi gifted his rent-receiving interest to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 who in turn granted pattern in respect of some portion of suit land to the defendant No. 3. The defendant Nos. 1 to 3 have never got possession of the suit land. Rs. 2480/- is still due on account of mortgage money. Hence the suit to recover this amount by selling the mortgaged property in auction if the decretal due be not paid. 

 3. It may be noted that in the suit the plaintiff No. 2 and the defendant No. 4 are the same person, namely, Nawab Ali Ahmed. As plaintiff he claims to be one of the successors to the assignee of the mortgage and as defendant No. 4 he is the mortgagor himself. 

 5. The learned Munsif held that the plaintiff No. 1 and the defendant No. 4 could be the same person in the suit and the suit cannot be held to be not maintain-able on that account. He held that the suit was filed within 12 years from the date of last payment of interest by the mortgagor Nawab Ali Ahmed and so was not barred by limitation, that the claim was not excessive, that the plaintiffs have possession in the suit land and that the defendants have no possession in it. The learned Munsif decreed the suit in the preliminary form. On appeal by the defendant No. 1, 2 and 7 the learned Subordinate Judge held that the appeal by the defendant Nos. 1 and 7 was not maintainable as they did not con  the suit in the trial Court and that their attorney cannot prefer an appeal without showing any cogent reason for non-appearance in the trial Court. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge agreed with the trial Court that the suit cannot be held to be not maintainable because the plaintiff No. 2 and defendant No. 4 are the same person, that the suit is not barred by limitation as it has been filed within 1 2 years of the last date of endorsement, that the question as to who possessed the suit land is not material for the determination of the issues involved in this case, and that the plaintiffs are entitled to the recovery of the mortgage money. The defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 7 are the appellant, in this appeal. 

 20. Mr. Mannan submits that Nawab Ali Ahmed's inclusion in the suit as plaintiff No. 2 was a necessity because the mortgage debt being invisible only one out of two successors to the assignee of the mortgage cannot enforce the mortgage. His presence in the suit as defendant No. 4 was also necessary for fuller and effective adjudication of the matters in issue. I agree with Mr. Mannan's submission that Nawab Ali Ahmed is a necessary party as a plaintiff. But when his presence is secured in the suit as a co-plaintiff, he has submitted for the Court's adjudication all matters regarding his rights and liabilities in respect of the mortgaged property. By making himself a defendant, an anomalous position has been created. He is suing himself for the mortgage money. If he loses as a plaintiff he can appeal. If he loses as a defendant he can appeal on contradictory grounds. The frame of the suit under such circumstances renders it non-maintainable in my opinion.
